title: Graph Mamba: Towards Learning on Graphs with State Space Models

problem.claim: Existing message-passing graph neural networks suffer from over-squashing and poor capture of long-range dependencies, while graph transformers have quadratic computational cost, lack inductive biases on graph structures, and rely on complex positional encodings.

gap.claim: It is unclear how to obtain the practical benefits associated with transformers, complex message passing, and positional encodings using state space models for graph-structured data.

contributions.claim: The paper presents Graph Mamba Networks, a framework for graph neural networks based on selective state space models.
The paper identifies four steps for designing Graph Mamba Networks: neighborhood tokenization, token ordering, state space model encoder architecture, and local encoding.
The paper provides theoretical justification for the power of Graph Mamba Networks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that Graph Mamba Networks attain outstanding performance across various benchmark datasets.
The authors state that code is available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph neural networks use local message passing, while graph transformers provide an alternative with different computational and structural tradeoffs.
The limitations of message passing and graph transformers motivate investigating state space models for graph learning.
The paper introduces Graph Mamba Networks and specifies four design steps for adapting selective state space models to graph data.
The paper reports theoretical justification and strong benchmark performance for Graph Mamba Networks.

source_observation.claim: The proposed framework decomposes graph adaptation of state space models into tokenization, ordering, encoder architecture, and local encoding.

interpretation.claim: Explicitly separating graph-specific representation choices from sequence-model architecture may clarify how non-sequential models can use state space mechanisms.

application.claim: When adapting sequence models to structured data, define the structural tokenization, ordering, encoder, and local-context components separately.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this decomposition transfers to graph types, tasks, or datasets beyond those evaluated.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the benchmark datasets or report quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the theoretical assumptions or guarantees.
The abstract does not specify the experimental baselines, tasks, or evaluation conditions.
The abstract does not provide the code link itself.
